methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
ACSL, a Tokyo-listed public company in the Drones & Autonomous sector founded by Kenzo Nonami, presents a narrow valuation foundation. The comparable universe consists of six private firms in the sector—Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air among them—with zero public peers identified in the same space.

The peer-median approach is not applicable here. The Drones & Autonomous sector contains only five same-sector comparables overall, and filtering for stage-matched, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers yielded fewer than three datapoints in each category. A median derived from the full sector set would introduce substantial methodological bias given ACSL's public status and the heterogeneous scale and business models of available private comps.

Without sufficient peer density to support triangulation via comparable multiples, valuation of ACSL requires alternative approaches not detailed in the available data. The primary constraint is the mismatch between ACSL's public market listing and the overwhelmingly private composition of its sector peer set, combined with insufficient narrow-filter coverage. Key uncertainties center on revenue scaling, unit economics relative to the private cohort, and the discount or premium justified by public listing status. Further analysis would require revenue multiples, profitability metrics, or DCF-based methodologies outside the scope of peer triangulation.
